papers.title: Bayesian transfer for offline Q-learning with multi-task Gaussian processes
papers.reason: The paper is mainly an offline reinforcement learning method, but its application to human decision-making data gives it a tangential connection to computational modelling of cognition.

papers.title: Pixels over Symbols: Sensory Realism Improves Behavioral Alignment in Models of Cognition
papers.reason: The paper centrally compares computational models of human cognition on visual working-memory and memory-dependent decision-making tasks using human behavioural alignment.

papers.title: Trail Making Tests in Extended Reality: A Critical Review with Implications for Cognitive Ageing
papers.reason: The review is substantially relevant to digital cognitive assessment of ageing and impairment using XR versions of an executive-function test, though it is not itself a multimodal classification study.

papers.title: The Clinical Profile and Bedside Clues of Anti-LGI1 Encephalitis Presenting With Isolated Cognitive Impairment: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.reason: The paper concerns clinical cognitive impairment in humans, but the title gives no specific indication of planning, working memory, attention, cognitive control, or computational assessment.

papers.title: Economic and psychological analysis of creative strategies in the cognitive model of managerial leadership
papers.reason: The paper proposes a conceptual cognitive model of managerial decision-making under uncertainty, but it is not a computational or empirically grounded model of executive function.

papers.title: From Human-Centered Firms to Hybrid Human-AI Organizations: Rethinking Organizational Design, Decision Rights, and Distributed Agency
papers.reason: The paper is about organizational design for autonomous AI agents rather than human or animal cognition or executive function.

papers.title: An Analytical Study on the Utility of Meditation for Student Life
papers.reason: The paper discusses meditation-related effects on attention, working memory, self-regulation, and prefrontal-attention networks, but it is a broad qualitative review rather than a focused empirical or modelling study of executive function.

papers.title: Social cognition and executive functions in parents of children with autism: a case-control study using an affective stroop fMRI paradigm
papers.reason: The title indicates a human case-control fMRI study of executive function and social cognition using an affective Stroop paradigm, directly relevant to neural and behavioural mechanisms of cognitive control.

papers.title: Progressive task-oriented extended reality in a cognitive stimulation programme for older adults with mild or early cognitive impairment: a pragmatic clinical trial of patient adaptation, usability and cognitive-functional outcomes
papers.reason: The paper studies XR-based cognitive stimulation and cognitive outcomes in older adults with mild cognitive impairment, but it is primarily an intervention feasibility trial rather than an executive-function model or diagnostic biomarker study.

papers.title: Validity, diagnostic accuracy, and feasibility of trail making test in virtual reality for mild cognitive impairment
papers.reason: The paper validates a VR Trail Making Test for distinguishing MCI from healthy ageing, making it highly relevant to digital task-based assessment of executive function and clinical status.

papers.title: Altered cognitive-motor integration in Mild Cognitive Impairment during a Virtual Driving Dual-Task: A Multimodal EEG-fNIRS Study
papers.reason: The title indicates a multimodal EEG-fNIRS study of MCI during a virtual driving dual-task, closely matching digital and neurophysiological assessment of cognitive control under dual-task demands.
